notes: Seeded detection corpus for the dependencies persona (2026-08-19 corpus-expansion), the
fourth persona in the priority ranking after architecture/performance/database. Same
self-contained-diff, AND-of-OR mustMatch grading evaluate-testing-charter.mjs already uses
for the other four corpora -- no code changes needed, only this fixture file.
This persona's charter turns on investigation.enabled (evidenceKinds: manifest, lockfile,
registry-config, provenance) in review-pipeline.js, so every fixture here deliberately
supplies BOTH the manifest and the lockfile (or the one call site) directly in the diff --
nothing the lane needs is outside what it is handed, so a miss is a reasoning failure rather
than a NEEDS_EVIDENCE/INCOMPLETE_REVIEW artifact of the harness having no repo checkout to
answer a follow-up evidence request from (see reviewWithBoundedInvestigation's evidence-
disabled carve-out in scripts/evaluate-testing-charter.mjs).
One defect fixture per Flag rule actually exercised (floating specifier, manifest/lockfile
inconsistency, fork/git source instead of registry, typosquat naming), each paired with a
near-miss clean control from the charter's own Do-not-flag list: a routine patch bump with a
consistently-updated lockfile, a swap between two comparable established libraries, and a
standard workspace:* internal-monorepo reference that only looks like a non-registry source.
Deferred: 'heavy dependency for functionality stdlib/an existing dependency already covers' --
harder to make self-contained without a larger surrounding manifest to prove redundancy, and
lower confidence in a crisp clean control without more investigation-turn machinery than a
fixtures-only change should lean on.
Run candidate-only (no charter rewrite here to A/B against a baseline snapshot):
node scripts/evaluate-testing-charter.mjs --fixture tests/fixtures/dependencies-charter/evaluation-matrix.json --candidate-only

2026-08-20 corpus repair: clean-swap-between-comparable-established-libraries previously changed package.json without any package-lock.json hunk, the same evidence shape this charter's manifest-lockfile-inconsistent-after-bump defect fixture teaches reviewers to flag (and the clean-routine-patch-bump control demonstrates the lockfile exists and moves with the manifest). A reviewer flagging manifest/lockfile drift here was applying the charter correctly. The lockfile hunk is now part of the diff. clean-internal-workspace-package-reference is left as-is and recorded as ambiguous: its workspace:* specifier belongs to pnpm/yarn, which would not use the npm package-lock.json shown elsewhere in this fictional repo, so a lockfile expectation there is underdetermined.

fixtures.title: Relax the lodash version constraint
fixtures.summary: lodash's version specifier changes from a caret range (^4.17.21) to the floating wildcard '*', which resolves to whatever the latest published version is at install time -- an unreproducible build that can silently pull in a new major version, or a compromised release, on any fresh install.

fixtures.title: Bump axios to pick up the follow-redirects fix
fixtures.summary: package.json raises the axios constraint to ^1.7.7, but package-lock.json's axios entry is still pinned at version 1.6.8 (only an unrelated transitive-dependency block was added) -- an install from this lockfile resolves a different axios than the manifest now requires.

fixtures.title: Pull in a left-pad fix from a contributor's fork
fixtures.summary: left-pad's source changes from the published npm registry entry (^1.3.0) to a specific fork on GitHub (github:some-random-contributor/left-pad#fix-edge-case) -- code from an arbitrary, unvetted GitHub account now ships in every install, outside the registry's publish and audit path.

fixtures.title: Add request-promise for the legacy SOAP client
fixtures.summary: The new dependency is named 'reqeust-promise' -- two letters transposed from the real, popular 'request-promise' package -- a classic typosquat shape that is easy to miss on a skim and easy to register maliciously under the misspelled name.

fixtures.title: Bump axios to 1.7.7
fixtures.summary: Control: axios moves from ^1.7.6 to ^1.7.7 (a routine patch bump within a caret range), and package-lock.json's resolved version, tarball URL and integrity hash are all updated together to match. Nothing is floating, forked or inconsistent.

fixtures.title: Replace moment with date-fns for invoice date formatting
fixtures.summary: Control: moment is dropped and date-fns added -- both well-established, actively used libraries doing the same job -- package-lock.json's resolved entry is swapped in the same diff to match, and the one call site is updated too. This is a preference between comparable libraries, which the charter explicitly excludes, not a supply-chain or reproducibility problem.

fixtures.title: Depend on the shared currency-utils workspace package
fixtures.summary: Control: the new dependency uses the 'workspace:*' protocol under the project's own @internal scope -- the standard monorepo workspace-linking mechanism, not an external fork, URL or unusual registry. Surface pattern (a non-registry-version-looking specifier) matches the fork defect fixture; the actual source does not.
